name: Transitional E-Bike, up to 500 W
description: An e-bike New South Wales lets be ridden as a bicycle until the end of February 2029 without complying with EN 15194: a pedal cycle whose motor of no more than 500 W continuous rated power assists less past 6 km/h and cuts out at 25 km/h, or above 6 km/h once the rider stops pedalling. The national 200 W power-assisted pedal cycle is allowed until the same day.

restrictions.rule: Two or more wheels, built to be propelled by human power through a belt, chain or gears, with an auxiliary motor
A maximum continuous rated power of 500 W
The motor's output progressively reduces as it speeds up past 6 km/h, and cuts off at 25 km/h, or once the rider stops pedalling above 6 km/h
One exceeding these limits is illegal even if software, an app or a switch restricts its power or speed
Not a bicycle from 1 March 2029, when only an e-bike complying with EN 15194 is
Since 21 August 2026 police and authorised officers may seize an illegal e-bike ridden on a road or road-related area and dispose of it
